founded_evidence: It was on December 16, 2005, that Houston officially welcomed the former San Jose Earthquakes to the city.
name: Houston Dynamo Football Club
notes: Revenue, operating income (Forbes' EBITDA-style measure) and value are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season from the list of 13 Feb 2026, cited via the Wayback Machine copy because forbes.com refuses scripted fetches; Forbes names Ted Segal as key owner. MLS clubs publish no accounts, so wages, pre-tax result and net debt are blank. Capacity is the club's own figure (20,656 seats); other listings carry 22,039. The club arrived from San Jose on 16 December 2005 and played its first season in 2006; honours also include the U.S. Open Cup in 2018 and 2023 (SportsLogos). Houston Dynamo Football Club is the organisation's name and covers the Dynamo, the NWSL's Houston Dash, Shell Energy Stadium operations and Houston Sports Park. The Dash are for sale: PJT Partners was retained in January 2025, talks to sell them to RHC Group for about $120m ended amid NWSL due diligence, and the process was relaunched in March 2026 (Sportico); a sale would separate the Dash from the Dynamo. No stake percentages are published. The club's legal entity was not found on a citable page, nor were attendance or social follower counts (SBJ gives only a +4% attendance change for 2025).

ownership_summary: Ted Segal, founder of real-estate firm EJS Group, has been majority owner and chairman since buying control from Gabriel Brener in June 2021 (a reported $400m deal including the NWSL's Houston Dash and the stadium lease); in August 2022 he bought out Brener, Oscar De La Hoya and Ben Guill. Minority owners are vice chairman Lyle Ayes (founder and CEO of Verance Capital, an equity investor since 2022), James Harden (since 2019) and Tim Howard (2024, at a reported $700m valuation). No institutional fund is named as a holder.
